prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Conroe, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported wrist fracture. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1478; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Evidence goes against the account: a nearby camera shows no collision at that place and time.
- The damage does not match the story: the dents are on another side and at another height than the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
On arrival at the scene in Conroe, Texas, I found two vehicles involved in a low-speed head-on collision. Driver 1 remained seated in the vehicle and reported pain in the left wrist, stating that it struck the steering wheel during the impact. The force of the collision appeared consistent with that type of injury. Driver 2 reported no injuries. A Passenger was in Driver 1's vehicle and confirmed that Driver 1 was inside during the crash, and the witnesses at the scene gave the same account.

On inspection, the dents on Driver 1's vehicle were on the side and at a height that did not match the frontal impact described. A nearby camera showed no collision at that location during the time reported. No earlier damage to Driver 1's vehicle is known from available records. Driver 1 is named on the policy covering the vehicle. Further review of the camera footage and the damage pattern is recommended before the account is accepted.
